iconicAnchor.label: Twentieth-century British studio pottery from Bernard Leach through Lucie Rie and Hans Coper
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The V&A frames studio pottery as individual workshop practice distinct from factory art pottery, spanning functional ware, expressive glaze, modernist refinement, and sculptural vessel form.

sources.title: Studio Pottery: an introduction
supports: Studio pottery is distinguished from pottery made by larger manufacturers and includes both useful objects and more sculptural investigations.
Modern studio potters developed organic and architectural forms through individual practice, material experiment, and new approaches to clay.

sources.title: Lucie Rie: a Modernist revolution in British studio ceramics
supports: Lucie Rie's refined simple forms and experimental glazes demonstrate that a handmade studio aesthetic need not look rustic or show throwing rings.
In Rie's work, surface decoration, glaze, incised line, and vessel form were integrated rather than applied as unrelated effects.
